A.claim: Unified: if 3 | gcd(x,y,z) or 4 | gcd(x,y,z), then A^x + B^y = C^z has no positive solutions. Packages the 3|x,3|y,3|z family (FLT3) and the 4|x,4|y,z even family (not_fermat_42).

B.claim: Consolidated necessary conditions on any Beal counterexample, kernel-verified: the bases are pairwise coprime; A != B; the exponents are not all divisible by 3; x and y are not both divisible by 4 with z even; and neither 3 nor 4 divides gcd(x,y,z). Together with exponent reduction: if a counterexample exists, one exists with all exponents in {4} u
